fixes.explanation: A city of refuge is a real thing in Moses' speech, friend, but it isn't where this verse sends a hard case. Moses says you must go up to the place the LORD your God will choose, and then you go to the Levitical priests and the judge who presides at that time (Deuteronomy 17:8-9). That's a whole different trip. Picture taking your hard case to the wrong building. You'd stand in line, get all the way to the window, and hear "wrong department." I've been sent to the back of a drawer, and even I know to check the address first.

True, baker. The king is to write himself a copy of the instruction and read from it all the days of his life, "so that he may learn to fear the LORD his God by carefully observing all the words of this instruction and these statutes" (Deuteronomy 17:19). Then Moses says, "…his heart will not be exalted above his countrymen…" (Deuteronomy 17:20). So the scroll isn't just for owning, it's for learning and observing. A king who copies it by hand and keeps coming back to it? That's a king getting his heart humbled one page at a time.
